statement: There is an absolute δ0 > 0 with the following property. Fix σ > 0 and take the severity E sufficiently large in terms of σ and the fixed profile. Assume the hypotheses of Lemma 6.3, with δ ≤ δ0, and also 1 2 ≤ κ ≤ 1.1, H ≥ σ, G = G0 + Ge, |∂[j] Ge| ≤ δ/H (0 ≤ j ≤ 2) in its scaled affine axes. Here G = ∂ ¯ ∂ψ and ∂[j] denotes any real or complex metric jet of order j, measured as a multilinear operator. Suppose either λ = 1, or H ≥ ME(1 + log λ)2 , (6.10) where ME is sufficiently large depending only on the fixed profile and E. Then the constant-center fiber potential defines a positive metric with nonpositive real sectional curvature. Its spatial Schur complement satisfies h ≥ cV . 33 More precisely, in scaled spatial axes and the tilted logarithmic fiber coordinate of Lemma 4.2, the contraction of its negative curvature on each Hermitian rank-at-most-two matrix with blocks (T, b, tf ) is bounded below by c  At2 f + W(b, b̄) + λ + τ H |T|2 + P|T|2 G  , (6.11) where c > 0 can be fixed independently of dimension and the stage parameters once the stated thresholds hold. The coefficient A and the form W are those of Lemma 4.2.
